page: Microsoft Azure E128-32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Easv7 family, featuring a constrained-vCPU configuration tailored for memory-intensive workloads that require lower core counts for software licensing or architectural efficiency. Managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI. The server features 1024.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 32.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is included, and no GPUs are present.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-thread execution paired with substantial memory capacity. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core testing at 3789.97 and single-threaded gzip compression at 41.52 GB/sec, alongside strong PassMark CPU scores of 57357.48. Multi-core performance sits in the middle tier at 59904.22 in stress-ng, consistent with its 32-vCPU core allocation. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 102.69 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 67.95 GB/sec for large block writes. In AI inference tasks, small language models exhibit top-tier generation rates of 403.93 tokens/sec, but throughput drops significantly on 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

The primary hardware tradeoff of this instance is the deliberate restriction of compute cores relative to memory footprint, coupled with the lack of ephemeral local NVMe storage. Economically, this architecture optimizes licensing expenditure for software engines billed on a per-core basis, allowing operators to leverage a full terabyte of memory without paying for unnecessary compute capacity. Microsoft Azure E128-32as_v7 is suited for massive in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching deployments, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-heavy analytical processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E128-32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Easv7 series, delivering an expansive 1024.0 GB RAM allocation across 32 dedicated vCPUs. Powered by 16 physical cores of an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor reaching up to 4.5 GHz, the instance provides 32.0 GB of memory per vCPU alongside 32 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction support. The configuration includes zero local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Synthetic evaluations demonstrate top-tier single-core performance and rapid compression rates, while overall multi-core throughput aligns with the 32-thread boundary. By decoupling high memory capacity from massive core counts, the instance offers architectural cost efficiency for systems constrained by per-core software licensing. It is targeted at large-scale in-memory databases, in-memory caching clusters, enterprise resource planning platforms, and intensive data processing workloads.
